source.title: Looped GPT-BERT: Trading Parameters for Computation in Small Language Modeling
source.authors: Ting-Shuo Fan; Hong-Tao Mu; Tian-Yun Zhou; Han-Sen Liu; Tao Ji

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It varies recurrent depth at fixed looped-model parameter count and reports pretraining-loss curves, conceptually testing whether an architecture/computation change has only a small effect on loss. It does not reproduce a scaling-law fit.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work as background but does not fit power laws or test scaling across orders of magnitude. Table 8's downstream task scores are not measures of downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. The loss values in Figure 1 are plotted without extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation. The study fits no power law and spans no orders of magnitude. Its loop-count ablation changes per-token compute through parameter sharing, not shape at a fixed parameter count with fixed compute, so it does not measure what V4 names. The only loss evidence is training loss over 10 epochs of a 7.48M-word corpus, which is repeated data rather than held-out loss. It is shown in a figure with no readable values.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that reusing four layers for twelve loops gives a 12.18M model whose training objective is close to a 29.9M non-looped model's. Loops preserve or improve selected syntactic scores but hurt Entity Tracking, and loop gains saturate quickly and vary by task. They stress this is a parameter-efficiency study, not a FLOP-matched one, limited to about 12M parameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates recurrent parameter sharing and loop-count ablations in a small-data language model, rather than fitting loss-scaling laws or searching compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Training loss changes with loop count; the text says the largest improvement is from 4 × 1 to 4 × 3 and later gains are smaller. Downstream outcomes also vary with objective ratio and task.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 12.18M parameters with four physical layers, more loop iterations lower training loss. The largest drop is from 4x1 to 4x3, with diminishing returns after that (Fig. 1, Sec. 4.4). The authors also say the 4x12 training objective is close to a 29.9M non-looped model's.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent depth through shared-layer looping, at fixed parameter count, lowers training loss with diminishing returns in loop count, in small data-limited LMs.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Second BabyLM Workshop
record.problems: The relevant loss evidence is plotted without numeric values and is training loss, not held-out loss. Each run uses one random seed; the authors note that small differences may fall within training variance. The study is limited to a small model, one cleaned corpus, and a narrow architecture range.
record.rows_left_out: Table 8 reports downstream task metrics across objective ratios and loop counts, but these do not measure any tested claim version: the study does not test downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. Other optimization ablations concern learning-rate choices rather than the claim versions.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 label is dropped. Looping varies compute at fixed parameters rather than shape at fixed parameters and compute. The loss is training loss on 10-epoch repeated data, and the numbers are figure-only. Downstream scores in Table 8 vary by loop count and objective but do not test V6, since no scale or loss predictability is assessed. All runs use a single seed.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute; no power-law fit.
No small-run fit or prediction of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget search for an optimal parameter/token allocation or fitted growth trends.
Tests loop count with four physical layers, not a broad range of depth, width, and other architecture choices; reports training curves rather than held-out loss.
English text pretraining only; no other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law test.
Reports downstream task scores for architectural variants but does not test whether those scores improve predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending.

reader_labels.reason: The text reports that training loss falls as loop count rises, with the largest improvement from 4 × 1 to 4 × 3 and smaller gains thereafter, but the plotted values are not numeric and the tested architecture range is narrow (R1–R4).
